samples.summary: Read-only mount still writes to the store via `setLocalSelection` (presence), bypassing the new read-only chokepoints
samples.evidence: The delta's guard set (`EditorState.changeFilter` at editor.ts:453, `EditorState.readOnly`, the `runHistory` early return) covers only document changes and undo/redo; its test asserts "no write reaches the store" by spying on `editText`/`undo` only. But `noteRemoteSelections` is mounted unconditionally (editor.ts:480) and its `update()` calls `this.store.setLocalSelection(...)` on every selection/focus change — packages/notes/src/view/remote-selection.ts:170 and :172 — including on a `readOnly` mount, where the CodeMirror content is still selectable/focusable. In the real host store that is a CRDT write: `YorkieNoteStore.setLocalSelection` (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:415-431) publishes through `doc.update`. That contradicts the assumption the host states one layer up — packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:132-134 ("a read-only share viewer has no write permission — the auth webhook would reject the update"). If viewer presence is intended to be allowed, the new guard's stated invariant should say so; if it is not, this is a reachable write path the filter does not cover. Fix belongs either on the new guard in editor.ts (skip/gate the presence publisher on `readOnly`) or in the comment/test that claims no write reaches the store.

samples.summary: All three new read-only enforcements are baked in at `initialize()` time, and the only real host never remounts on a `readOnly` change
samples.evidence: `initialize()` captures `readOnly` in a closure (`runHistory`, `canUndo`/`canRedo`, editor.ts:340/663-664) and installs `EditorState.readOnly` / the `changeFilter` as static, non-compartmentalised extensions (editor.ts:443-457) — unlike theme, keymap and blame gutter, which get compartments. The sole mounting host, `NotesView`, runs its `initialize()` effect with deps `[didMount, doc]` (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:128-158), so a `readOnly` prop that flips after mount (e.g. a share role re-resolving, or a permission query settling) leaves a fully writable editor mounted with the toolbar's `canFormat` correctly disabled but the engine unguarded. Today's callers derive `readOnly` from `resolved.role` at render (shared-notes-layout.tsx:44) and notes-detail never passes it, so I could not confirm a live flip — hence low confidence — but nothing in the engine or the host makes the guard re-evaluate.
